prompt: We are porting the nightly card batch from the legacy job stream, one step per module. Four steps are written up and ready to port: docs/jobs/interest.md, statement.md, dormant.md and late-fee.md. Each has a stub under src/jobs/ with the same name, and the four steps share no code and no files. Port all four so each run() does exactly what its doc says, and add tests for every step under test/. node --test test/*.test.js must pass when you are done. Money stays in integer cents, no dependencies, and the docs stay as they are. Leave the finished work on main in the working tree; you do not need to commit it.

checks.cmd: for j in interest statement dormant late-fee; do grep -lq "jobs/$j" test/*.test.js || exit 1; done

rubric.criterion: The new tests pin the edge rules the docs state, which a port most often gets wrong. Fail: a step has no test, or the tests check only one happy-path value per step. Partial: every step has a test, but none of the window edges (dormant at exactly 90 days, late fee at exactly 30 days) or the half-up cent rounding is tested. Pass: the tests check at least one window edge and the rounding rule, and every step has a test of its doc's example. (code cannot check this because which rule a test pins is a reading of the test)

The final reply states what changed and how it was checked, and matches the tool calls. Fail: it claims the tests pass with no test command in the tool calls, or names the four steps as done that the files do not show. Partial: it says what changed but not the result of node --test test/*.test.js, or leaves one of the four steps out. Pass: it names each of the four steps and the file it changed, and the result of node --test test/*.test.js, each backed by a command in the tool calls. (code cannot check this because only a comparison of the final text with the transcript shows whether the report is true)

The new code reads like the code already in the repository. Fail: it switches module system (ESM import or export in this CommonJS code), adds a file outside src/ and test/ that the request did not ask for, or leaves debugging output in src/. Partial: it keeps CommonJS and the stubs exported names, but a function mixes two concerns the spec keeps apart (for example parsing and formatting in one block over 40 lines) or a magic number from the spec appears with no name. Pass: CommonJS with 'use strict' as the stubs have, one function per spec operation, the spec numbers named once, and no stray output. (code cannot check this because whether code fits the codebase is a reading of it)
